verdict: BigBear.ai grew revenue 31% to $43.6M, almost all of it from the US government, but a $76.7M goodwill impairment charge drove a $91.9M net loss.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP, diluted)
kpis.note: vs a $0.01 basic profit per share a year ago

kpis.label: Gross margin
kpis.note: Up from 22% a year ago, as revenue grew faster than delivery costs

segments.name: U.S. government
segments.note: AI decision-intelligence software and services for US defense, intelligence and other federal customers — the core of the business.

opex.name: Goodwill impairment
opex.note: A one-off write-down of goodwill — the premium paid for past acquisitions — after the company concluded that part of it is no longer worth what the books said (non-cash).

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Running the company — executives, finance, legal and admin, plus selling costs. Up from $25.3M a year ago.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Building its AI products and platforms. Up from $3.4M a year ago.

opex.name: Restructuring charges
opex.note: Small remaining costs from restructuring plans.

otherDetail: Interest income of $3.821M and a $4.228M gain from the change in fair value of derivative liabilities, less $0.307M of interest expense and $0.204M of other expense, for net other income of $7.538M.

takeaways.title: Government work drove solid growth
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 31% to $43.6M. US government customers grew 34% to $39.2M — 90% of the total — while non-US government and commercial work grew 10% to $4.3M. Gross margin improved to 31% from 22%.

takeaways.title: An impairment, not operations, caused the loss
takeaways.text: The quarter includes a $76.7M goodwill impairment — a non-cash write-down of value from past acquisitions. Without it, the operating loss would have been about $23.2M instead of $100.0M. General and admin costs of $31.3M remain high relative to $43.6M of revenue.

takeaways.title: Bottom line, with a small tax benefit
takeaways.text: Interest income and a $4.2M gain on derivative liabilities softened the loss, and taxes were a $0.6M benefit rather than a cost. The net loss was $91.9M, or $0.19 a share, versus a small profit a year ago. Nine-month operating cash outflow was $49.8M.

oneTimers: Goodwill impairment of $76.7M in the quarter (the same amount for the nine months) — a non-cash charge that accounts for most of the net loss.
A $4.2M gain from the change in fair value of derivatives (warrant and note liabilities) is a mark-to-market move, not cash earned.
footerNote: BigBear.ai reports in thousands; figures are shown in $M with decimals so the lines add up exactly. The company reports a single operating segment, so revenue is split by customer type, as disclosed in its Form 10-Q. This is a loss quarter: the shortfall is covered by cash on hand.
